Data.title: Waste Management And Overall Recycling Rates, Annual
Data.datasource: MINISTRY OF SUSTAINABILITY AND THE ENVIRONMENT, NATIONAL ENVIRONMENT AGENCY
Data.footnote: From 2019, wood and horticultural wastes recycled include materials that are sent to facilities (e.g., biomass power plants and Sembcorp's Energy from Waste plant) for use as fuel.  Data in this table are rounded to the nearest thousand tonnes and percentage point.

row.footnote: Data are used for SDG 12.3.1 '(a) Food loss index and (b) food waste index'.  Please refer to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) Global Metadata (https://unstats.un.org/sdgs/metadata) for more information on SDG 12.3.1.

The drop in overall recycling rate in 2020 was largely due to the substantially smaller amounts of Ferrous Metal scrap and Construction and Demolition waste generated and recycled.  While the recycling rates for these two waste streams did not change, a drop in the quantities of these waste streams affected the overall recycling rate as they make up a significant portion of the waste mix.  The lower recycling rate of paper/cardboard also contributed to the lower overall recycling rate because recyclables collection programmes by Public Waste Collectors were halted during the Circuit Breaker in Singapore (April to June 2020).  Data are used for SDG 12.5.1 'National recycling rate, tons of material recycled'.
